claim: Vertebrate kidneys play two evolutionary conserved roles in waste excretion and osmoregulation.
source: The vertebrate kidneys play two evolutionary conserved roles in waste excretion and osmoregulation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about vertebrate kidney function.

claim: The kidney of fish is considered as a functional ortholog of mammalian bone marrow that serves as a hematopoietic hub for generating blood cell lineages and immunological responses.
source: Besides, the kidney of fish is considered as a functional ortholog of mammalian bone marrow that serves as a hematopoietic hub for generating blood cell lineages and immunological responses.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge in the field, though the authors note that details remain to be elucidated.

claim: The study generated a comprehensive atlas with 59 hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC) and immune-cells types from zebrafish kidneys via single-cell transcriptome profiling analysis.
source: To this end, our present study generated a comprehensive atlas with 59 hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC) and immune-cells types from zebrafish kidneys via single-cell transcriptome profiling analysis.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by the scRNA-seq data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The identified kidney cell populations included almost all known cells associated with innate and adaptive immunity.
source: These populations included almost all known cells associated with innate and adaptive immunity, and displayed differential responses to viral infection, indicating their diverse functional roles in antiviral immunity.
evidence: This is supported by the comprehensive cell type identification shown in Figures 1, 5, 6, and 7.

claim: The identified kidney cell populations displayed differential responses to viral infection.
source: These populations included almost all known cells associated with innate and adaptive immunity, and displayed differential responses to viral infection, indicating their diverse functional roles in antiviral immunity.
evidence: This is supported by data showing changes in cell abundance and gene expression after SVCV infection (Figures 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10).

claim: HSPCs were found to have extensive reactivities to viral infection.
source: Remarkably, HSPCs were found to have extensive reactivities to viral infection, and the trained immunity can be effectively induced in certain HSPCs.
evidence: This is supported by data showing changes in HSPC populations after SVCV infection (Figure 2D-E) and differential gene expression (Figure 10).

claim: Trained immunity can be effectively induced in certain HSPCs.
source: Remarkably, HSPCs were found to have extensive reactivities to viral infection, and the trained immunity can be effectively induced in certain HSPCs.
evidence: This is supported by data from the vaccinated+infected group showing enhanced HSPC responses (Figure 11).

claim: The antigen-stimulated adaptive immunity can be fully generated in the kidney.
source: In addition, the antigen-stimulated adaptive immunity can be fully generated in the kidney, suggesting the kidney acts as a secondary lymphoid organ.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing T and B cell activation, proliferation, and somatic hypermutation in the kidney (Figure 13).

claim: The kidney acts as a secondary lymphoid organ.
source: In addition, the antigen-stimulated adaptive immunity can be fully generated in the kidney, suggesting the kidney acts as a secondary lymphoid organ.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing adaptive immune responses in the kidney, which are characteristic of secondary lymphoid organs.

claim: The fish kidney is a dual-functional entity with functionalities of both primary and secondary lymphoid organs.
source: These results indicated that the fish kidney is a dual-functional entity with functionalities of both primary and secondary lymphoid organs.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined evidence of hematopoiesis (primary lymphoid organ function) and adaptive immune responses (secondary lymphoid organ function) occurring in the kidney.

claim: Teleost fish are the earliest living jawed vertebrates known as an important link in vertebrate evolution.
source: Teleost fish are a group of indispensable model organisms for comprehending the evolutionary history and general principles underlying the design of the vertebrate immune system, since they stand as the earliest living jawed vertebrates known as an important link in vertebrate evolution (Sunyer, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge in evolutionary biology, supported by citation.

claim: Teleost fish possess the fundamental components of both innate and adaptive immune systems, akin to those seen in humans and other mammalian counterparts.
source: Thus far, it was generally accepted that teleost fish possess the fundamental components of both innate and adaptive immune systems, akin to those seen in humans and other mammalian counterparts (Rauta et al., 2012; Secombes and Wang, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge in fish immunology, supported by citations.

claim: Bony fish represent the earliest living organisms endowed with a rudimentary adaptive immune system encompassing basic molecular and cellular constituents.
source: Evolutionarily speaking, bony fish represent the earliest living organisms endowed with a rudimentary adaptive immune system encompassing basic molecular and cellular constituents.
evidence: This is established knowledge in evolutionary immunology.

claim: Fishes lack bone marrow, histologically discernible lymph nodes, Peyer's patches, and germinal centers.
source: Notably absent in fishes are the bone marrow, histologically discernible lymph nodes, Peyer's patches, and germinal centers—entities that define primary and secondary lymphoid organs in mammals (Neely and Flajnik, 2016; Matz et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge about fish anatomy, supported by citations.

claim: Fishes lack antibody class-switch recombination activity.
source: Additionally, fishes lack antibody class-switch recombination activity, albeit retaining the ability to express activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) (Barreto et al., 2005; Wakae et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about fish immunology, supported by citations.

claim: Fishes retain the ability to express activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID).
source: Additionally, fishes lack antibody class-switch recombination activity, albeit retaining the ability to express activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) (Barreto et al., 2005; Wakae et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about fish immunology, supported by citations.

claim: The study classified splenic leukocytes into 11 principal categories and identified over 50 subset populations within these categories.
source: Our work has entailed the classification of splenic leukocytes into 11 principal categories and the identification of over 50 subset populations within these categories.
evidence: This refers to previous work by the authors, supported by citation (Hu et al., 2023).

claim: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) exist within the spleen.
source: Particularly noteworthy was our discovery of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) that existed within the spleen.
evidence: This refers to a previous finding by the authors, supported by citation (Hu et al., 2023).

claim: The fish spleen may function as a hematopoietic site, transcending its established role as a secondary lymphoid organ.
source: This observation intimates that the fish spleen may well function as a hematopoietic site, transcending its established role as a secondary lymphoid organ.
evidence: This is inferred from the discovery of HSPCs in the spleen.

claim: The study classified 13 categories of cells from kidney leukocyte preparations.
source: As a result, our classification efforts have yielded 13 categories of cells from kidney leukocyte preparations, unearthing 59 potential subset cells spanning HSPCs and immune cell-associated categories.
evidence: This is supported by the scRNA-seq data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The study identified 59 potential subset cells spanning HSPCs and immune cell-associated categories.
source: As a result, our classification efforts have yielded 13 categories of cells from kidney leukocyte preparations, unearthing 59 potential subset cells spanning HSPCs and immune cell-associated categories.
evidence: This is supported by the comprehensive subclustering analysis shown in Figures 2, 5, 6, 7, and 8.

claim: The observed subset populations manifest disparate reactions to SVCV infection.
source: The observed subset populations manifest disparate reactions to SVCV infection.
evidence: This is supported by data showing differential changes in cell abundance and gene expression across subsets after SVCV infection.

claim: Some HSPC subsets exhibit a robust proliferative response to viral infection.
source: Most notably, some HSPC subsets exhibit a robust proliferative response to viral infection, capable of inducing trained immunity.
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased abundance of cycling HSPCs (H1) after SVCV infection (Figure 2D-E).

claim: A comprehensive array of cells encompassing diverse antigen-presenting cells (APCs) as well as effector T and B cells integral for the full activation of adaptive immunity were identified within the kidney.
source: Furthermore, we have successfully identified a comprehensive array of cells—encompassing diverse antigen-presenting cells (APCs) as well as effector T and B cells—integral for the full activation of adaptive immunity within the kidney.
evidence: This is supported by the identification of various macrophage/DC subsets (Figure 7), T cell subsets (Figure 5), and B cell subsets (Figure 6).

claim: Adaptive immune-associated cells display marked responsiveness to SVCV infection and antigenic stimulation.
source: These adaptive immune-associated cells display marked responsiveness to SVCV infection and antigenic stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing changes in T and B cell populations after SVCV infection (Figures 6, 9) and experimental validation of T and B cell activation (Figure 13).

claim: The complete process of adaptive immunity unfolds within the kidney, as evidenced by the substantial expansion, activation, and somatic hypermutation (SHM) of antigen-specific T and B cells upon exposure to cognate antigens.
source: Evidently, the complete process of adaptive immunity unfolds within the kidney, as evidenced by the substantial expansion, activation, and somatic hypermutation (SHM) of antigen-specific T and B cells upon exposure to cognate antigens.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing T and B cell proliferation, activation marker expression, and SHM in the kidney after antigen stimulation (Figure 13).

source: Clusters 0, 2, and 9 were identified as neutrophils based on their expression of lineage marker genes including mpx, lyz, cpa5, cd11b, adgrg3, and nccrp1 (Figure 1C and D).

source: Cluster 1 was identified as a macrophage/myeloid population due to the expression of lineage-specific genes including mpeg1.1, ctss2.2, mpeg1.2, grn1, marco, and grna.

claim: Cluster 3 represented B cells, expressing lineage marker genes like ighm, ighd, ighz, igl3v5, cd79a, cd79b and cd37.
source: Cluster 3 represented B cells, expressing lineage marker genes like ighm, ighd, ighz, igl3v5, cd79a, cd79b and cd37 (Figure 1C and F).

claim: Mpeg1.1+ B cells exist in zebrafish kidney, gut, skin, and spleen tissues.
source: Consistent with the existence of Mpeg1.1+ B cells in zebrafish kidney, gut, skin, and spleen tissues (Ferrero et al., 2020), this cluster displayed expression of mpeg1.1.

claim: Clusters 4 and 6 corresponded to HSPCs 1 and HSPCs 2 populations, marked by the expression of pertinent signature genes.
source: Clusters 4 and 6 corresponded to HSPCs 1 and HSPCs 2 populations, marked by the expression of pertinent signature genes like nanos1, spi2, meis1b, foxp4, csf1rb, gtpbp4, rpl5b, rplp2l, rpl18, rps7, rsl1d1 in cluster 4, and mki67, mcm5, dut, npm1a, snu13b, cnbpa in cluster 6 (Figure 1C, I and J; Rubin et al., 2022).

claim: Cluster 5 represented T and NK cells, expressing T-cell signature genes and NK lineage genes.
source: Cluster 5 represented T and NK cells, expressing T-cell signature genes including trac, trbc, cd3ζ, lck, zap70, cd4-1, cd8a, runx3, il2rb, bcl11ba and il7r, as well as NK lineage genes like nkl.2, cd56, cd94, cd27 and zbtb32 (Figure 1C, G and H).

claim: Cluster 8 denoted the HSPCs 3 population, expressing zfpm1, meis1b, gata1a, zeb2a, tal1, mef2aa, mpl, pbx1a and hdr marker genes.
source: Cluster 8 denoted the HSPCs 3 population, expressing zfpm1, meis1b, gata1a, zeb2a, tal1, mef2aa, mpl, pbx1a and hdr marker genes (Figure 1C and K).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1C and K.

claim: hsp70 members are essential for the differentiation of hematopoietic progenitors into erythroids.
source: This HSPC population also actively expressed hsp70 (hsp70.1, hsp70l, hsp70.3), itga2b, thbs1b, hbaa1, hbaa2, hbba1, hbba1.1, and rgcc, among which hsp70 members are essential for the differentiation of hematopoietic progenitors into erythroids (Ribeil et al., 2007).

claim: Sub clustering of the three HSPC clusters unveiled 11 enrichments (designated as H0–H10).

evidence: This is supported by the t-SNE plot in Figure 2A showing 11 distinct HSPC subclusters.

source: Within this context, H0 manifested as a Nanos1+Spi2+ phenotypic cluster expressing signature genes nanos1 and spi2, alongside specific expressions of sla2, csf1rb, rn7sk, sik1, and irf1b, forming a collection of potential new marker genes (Figure 2A–C).

source: Meanwhile, H1 was identified as a group of cycling HSPCs, characterized by the expression of the marker gene mki67.

source: Cells within H6 represented myeloid progenitors, showing extensive expression of mmp13a.1, si:ch1073-429i10.1, il1b, cpa5, mpx, timp2b, BX908782.2, npsn, lect2l and lyz marker genes (Figure 2A–C).

claim: H7 and H8 were identified as erythrocyte and lymphoid progenitor populations.
source: H7 and H8 were identified as erythrocyte and lymphoid progenitor populations, denoted by their expression of hbba1.1, hbaa1, hbba1, si:ch211-5k11.8, hbba2, hbaa2, si:ch211-103n10.5, cahz, hemgn in H7, and pbx1a, pdpk1a, rag1, rag2, cxcr4b, h2afx, ccr9a, sid1, zgc:77784, nme3, kdm6bb in H8, respectively (Figure 2A–C).

source: The endothelial progenitors were also found in the bone marrow of mouse, and they are developmentally associated with a subset of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells, and can differentiate ex vivo to an endothelial phenotype (Asahara et al., 1997; Shi et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: There is substantial overlapping HSPCs and immune cell types in both the kidney and spleen.

source: In aggregate, our findings reveal overall similarities in HSCPs' composition and differentiation potentials between the kidney and spleen, suggesting analogous functionalities in hematopoiesis and immunity across both organs.

claim: Subdividing the T/NK category led to the observation of 23 subset clusters (designated as T0–T22).
source: Subdividing the T/NK category in Figure 1 led us to observe 23 subset clusters (designated as T0–T22) enriched within the T/NK population through iterative subclustering (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by the t-SNE plot in Figure 5A showing 23 distinct T/NK subclusters.

claim: Clusters T5, T17, and T18 were identified as NKT subsets due to their widespread expression of NKT lineage genes.
source: Notably, clusters T5, T17, and T18 were identified as NKT subsets due to their widespread expression of NKT lineage genes, including cd3ζ, trbc, cd8a/cd4-1, zbtb32, nkl.2, il2rb, and cd94 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Cluster T0 represented the CD3lowCD4lowCD8low T subset.
source: Cluster T0 represented the CD3lowCD4lowCD8low T subset due to its low expression of cd3ζ, cd4-1, and cd8a.

claim: The CD3lowCD4lowCD8low T subset likely represents an early developmental population of double positive (DP) T cells.
source: This subset likely represents an early developmental population of double positive (DP) T cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is inferred from the low expression of T cell markers.

claim: Clusters T1 and T2 were identified as CD8+-nkl.2 subsets exhibiting cytotoxic activity.
source: Clusters T1 and T2 were identified as CD8+-nkl.2 subsets exhibiting cytotoxic activity, as evidenced by the expression of cd8a and nkl.2 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T3 was classified as a Th1 subset based on its expression of Th1-specific genes.
source: T3 was classified as a Th1 subset based on its expression of Th1-specific genes, including cd4-1, ifng1, il2, cxcr3.1.1, tnfa, and tnfb.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T3 expressed the cytotoxic T cell-related gzmk gene, suggesting its potential for both helper and cytotoxic activities.
source: Additionally, T3 expressed the cytotoxic T cell-related gzmk gene, suggesting its potential for both helper and cytotoxic activities (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is inferred from the expression of both Th1 and cytotoxic markers.

claim: Clusters T6, T7, T10, T13, T19, T20, and T21 were categorized as NK subsets.
source: Continuing the narrative, clusters T6, T7, T10, T13, T19, T20, and T21 were categorized as NK subsets due to their expression of NK signature genes, including zbtb32, nkl.2, il2rb, and cd94 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T19, T7, and T6/10/13/20/21 represented CD11b−CD27−, CD11b+CD27+, and CD11b+CD27− subset NK cells.
source: Among these, T19 exhibited no expression of cd11b or cd27, T7 expressed both cd11b and cd27, and T6, T10, T13, T20, and T21 expressed cd11b but not cd27 (Figure 5C). These observations suggested that T19, T7, and T6/10/13/20/21 represented CD11b−CD27−, CD11b+CD27+, and CD11b+CD27− subset NK cells, demonstrating high differentiation potential, cytokine secretion, and cytolytic functions as observed in humans (Fu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C and comparison with human NK cell subsets.

claim: Clusters T8, T9, and T15 were identified as a group of CD8+ CTL subsets.
source: Clusters T8, T9, and T15 were identified as a group of CD8+ CTL subsets, expressing CD8+ CTL-specific genes, including cd8a, cd8b, gzma, gzmk, ifng1, and tnfb (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T11 was labeled as a γδ T subset due to its high expression of trgc, trdc, sox13, and cd3ζ.
source: T11 was labeled as a γδ T subset due to its high expression of trgc, trdc, sox13, and cd3ζ, combined with low expression of cd4-1 and cd8a.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T12 was classified as a Th17 subset due to its expression of lineage-specific genes.
source: T12 was classified as a Th17 subset due to its expression of lineage-specific genes, including roraa, stat3, il17a/f3, il21, cd4-1, ccr6a, rorc, cd3ζ, il22, tgfb1a, and il17a/f1.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T14 represented a distinctive CD4+IgM+ subset characterized by the concurrent expression of ighm and cd4-2.2.
source: T14 represented a distinctive CD4+IgM+ subset characterized by the concurrent expression of ighm and cd4-2.2.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T16 was designated as a regulatory T (Treg) subset based on the expression of foxp3a, foxp3b, ctla4, cd4-1, and il17ra1a marker genes.
source: Cluster T16 was designated as a regulatory T (Treg) subset based on the expression of foxp3a, foxp3b, ctla4, cd4-1, and il17ra1a marker genes (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: T21 was indicative of a Th2-like subset, demonstrated by its expression of Th2-associated genes.
source: T21 was indicative of a Th2-like subset, demonstrated by its expression of Th2-associated genes, including cd3ζ, il4, gata3, il13, stat6, batf, and cxcr4b.

claim: The Th2-like subset exhibited elevated expression of faslg, a pivotal apoptotic inducer contributing to T cell cytotoxicity.
source: Notably, this subset exhibited elevated expression of faslg, a pivotal apoptotic inducer contributing to T cell cytotoxicity (Figure 5C, Figure 9D).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 9D.

claim: B0 and B3 were designated as immature/mature B cells (im/mat. B) due to their expression of gata1a and zfpm1 genes.
source: B0 and B3 were designated as immature/mature B cells (im/mat. B) due to their expression of gata1a and zfpm1 genes (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: B1 was categorized as a canonical IgM+IgD+ B subset, characterized by its high expression of ighm and ighd genes.
source: B1 was categorized as a canonical IgM+IgD+ B subset, characterized by its high expression of ighm and ighd genes.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: B2 and B7 were identified as pro/pre B subsets, exhibiting significant expression of pclaf, pdia4, pdia6, rag1, and rag2 genes.
source: B2 and B7 were identified as pro/pre B subsets, exhibiting significant expression of pclaf, pdia4, pdia6, rag1, and rag2 genes.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: B4 likely represented a population of plasma cells that highly expressed ighm or ighz.
source: B4 likely represented a population of plasma cells that highly expressed ighm or ighz (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is inferred from the high expression of immunoglobulin genes.

source: B5 displayed expression of genes related to germinal-center B cells, including aicda (AID), mki67, top2a, stmn1a, bach2b, bcl6aa, bcl6ab, cd81a, cd9a, irf8, lmo2, pclaf, and nfkb2, which exhibited a notable increase following virus infection (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6A-C.

claim: Cluster B6 comprised activated B cells and plasmablasts (act. B/PBs).
source: Cluster B6 comprised activated B cells and plasmablasts (act. B/PBs), actively expressing dscamb, cpa5, fcer1g, mmp13a.1, mpx, timp2b, npsn, il1b, and lect2l.
